short: Standard on the adversarial loss (M02): it predates the paper in video-to-speech and its gains are small, with no variance reported; behind on evaluation (M12): no listening test.
position: The paper changes the training-only supervision (M02): a Patch-GAN discriminator adds an adversarial loss, weighted 0.25 against 0.75 MSE, to an ultrasound-to-mel 3D CNN. M02 is standard: the authors claim a first only for ultrasound, and a critic loss added to a regression loss for speech from a silent signal already existed in video-to-speech. The effect is not established: no repeated runs or variance are reported, and test STOI rises 0.24% relative in Hungarian and 1.8% in English (inference). The GAN model also has lower test MSE than the MSE-only model, which is unexplained: a weak baseline, a regularizing effect of the adversarial term, or the change from 1 to 5 output frames would each produce it (inference). Evaluation (M12) is behind on the group's own earlier practice: its 2020 study ran a MUSHRA test with 22 listeners, four earlier ultrasound-to-speech studies of the group ran MUSHRA (pattern match), and this one runs none, so improved quality rests on objective metrics only.
